fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so responders can distinguish it from adjacent openings or road features.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles and movable obstructions so emergency equipment can reach all structures without delay.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive so it does not narrow the travel width or reduce visibility for approaching vehicles.
• Post a site map or structure diagram near the driveway entrance showing the locations of all structures, the access drive, and any gates.
• Keep any gates across the access drive equipped with a Knox Box or standardized lock so responders can enter without delay.
• Identify and mark a turnaround point near the structures so large emergency vehicles can reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Clear a path around the rear of the structures wide enough for responders to move on foot with equipment.
• Trim dense vegetation that is directly adjacent to either detached structure to create open space between the plants and the buildings.
• Confirm that any rear gate or access point to the back of the property can be opened quickly and is not secured with an unfamiliar lock.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove or thin the cluster of trees closest to the structure to reduce direct fire contact with the building.
• Trim branches on scattered trees near the structure so they do not touch or hang over the roof or walls.
• Cut back shrubs that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Keep the driveway clear of low-hanging branches along its full length so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency responders arriving under poor visibility conditions.
• Clear any dead plant material or loose debris from the area immediately surrounding the structure.
• Remove any vegetation or stored materials from the rear of the structure that limit movement around the building.
